messages:
Maria L.: quick runway snapshot — heads-up: APAC promo next week looks like it could add ~28% GPU-hour demand on top of baseline. I ran a short sim and paused on recommendations. TL;DR: shift 12% of eu-west burst -> apac-southeast burst, keep canary on dedicated eu-north.
Jamal K.: thanks. is that based on historical promo multipliers or new marketing numbers?
Maria L.: marketing forecast + cookiecast derived uplift. baseline +35k GPU-hours/week; promo adds ~9k (range 7–12k). numbers in the sim: per-cluster qps and tail latency impact included.
Sasha P.: quick ask — any network constraints in apac-southeast? last time we moved load there we saw inter-region egress spikes and peering flaps.
Maria L.: good call. ops-bot posted peering alert yesterday — eu->apac egress throttling window 02:00–04:00 UTC is still showing increased drops (see logs). plan assumes no long egress throttles during peak; if throttles persist, fallback is to route through dedicated in us-west.
ops-bot: recent_peering_events: 2026-11-04 02:34Z (eu-west -> apac-southeast) 1.9% packet drop over 12m, BGP flaps: 2. See /infra/alerts/peering-3342.
Liam R.: cost/levers? if we move burst capacity to apac that increases committed spend. can we instead increase KV cache hit targets and squeeze more throughput?
Maria L.: modeled two levers: (A) reallocate burst (capex/spend shift) — +8% committed monthly but keeps avg latency low; (B) batching+cache optimizations — 6% token-cost reduction but adds ~40ms p95 for short chats. I attached the quick numbers below.
Jamal K.: paste the numbers? can we do mixed: lean on cache for non-critical routes and reserve burst for high-SLA customers?
Maria L.: exactly. excerpt from the sim:

```
Scenario A (realloc burst): +12k GPU-hours/week -> cost delta +$18k/wk, p95 < 220ms across apac clusters
Scenario B (cache+batching): +0 GPU-hours, token cost -6%, p95 +40ms (short chats)
Hybrid: +4k GPU-hours, cost +$6k/wk, p95 +10–15ms
```

Sasha P.: ACK. Hybrid looks sane. Ops question: do we have spare dedicated eu-north nodes to act as failover for canary during promos?
Aisha N.: quick inventory: eu-north dedicated pool has 6 nodes (2 reserved spare), burst pool can scale to +8 nodes fast but uses preemptible SKUs. If we need hard SLA we should reserve one extra dedicated slot (adds ~$3k/mo).
Liam R.: what about using spot-to-dedicated migration early in the promo window to reduce preempt risk? We can have a script that promotes spot -> reserved when sustained runrate > threshold.
Maria L.: I prototyped a promotion hook. snippet:

```
# pseudo
if sustained_gpu_hours(30m) > promo_threshold:
  trigger_migration(pool='apac-burst', target='apac-dedicated', min_nodes=2)
```

Need an SRE owner to wire this up and add rollback conditions.
Jamal K.: I can take ownership of the migration hook. will add a safeguard: only promote if average preempt rate < 5% and cost delta approved by finance.
Sasha P.: network mitigation — I'll open a short peering request with infra-net. also suggest adding a regional routing policy: prefer intra-zone cache for small requests, avoid cross-continent egress during 02:00–06:00 UTC.
Aisha N.: finance note: the hybrid scenario is within our promo runway but we should cap total burst spend to +$10k/wk; beyond that we need exec signoff.
Maria L.: action items:
- Jamal: implement/promote migration hook + PR with rollback (ETA: 48h)
- Sasha: peering request + routing policy draft (ETA: 24h)
- Liam: load test hybrid config in canary apac cluster (ETA: 36h)
- Aisha: confirm budget guardrail and set alert (ETA: 24h)
- ops-bot: emit a burn-rate metric alert if weekly GPU-hours > baseline*1.20

Jamal K.: picking this up. will post PR link when ready. @ops-bot can you add a synthetic that pings our canary route every 30s during promo window?
ops-bot: scheduled_synthetic created: canary-heartbeat-apac (30s), window: 2026-11-10 -> 2026-11-17, tags: promo-2026-nov
Maria L.: good. final call: hybrid + routing policy. we'll re-evaluate mid-promo and escalate to execs if spend > guardrail. thanks team :thumbsup:
Sasha P.: :+1: leaving a note to capture latency regression checks in the dashboard (per-route p95 + token cost delta).
